prerequisites: Fundamentals of information transfer and processing

learning_outcomes.text: The student can derive simple dynamic models of systems from a wide range of engineering disciplines: for example, electrical, mechanical, hydraulic, thermal, and chemical systems, as well as discrete-time systems.
The student can apply the basic methods for modeling, describing, and analyzing linear dynamic time-invariant systems in a discipline-independent manner and critically evaluate the results obtained.

The student can analyze a continuous-time and discrete-time system in both the time domain and the frequency domain, based on different model representations, such as a transfer function description, a state-space model.

For a given linear time-invariant system with one input and one output, based on specifications in the time domain or frequency domain, the student can design a classical feedback controller based on frequency domain methods (choice of controller type and determination of control parameters).

For a given linear time-invariant system with one input and one output, based on specifications in the time domain or frequency domain, the student can design a controller based on state feedback, including a closed-loop state estimator.

For a given linear time-invariant system with one input and one output, based on specifications in the time domain or frequency domain, the student can add feedforward to a classical controller or a state controller to eliminate steady-state errors for different types of reference signals.
For a given linear time-invariant system with one input and one output, based on specifications in the time domain or frequency domain, the student can critically evaluate the above designs.
The student can convert a continuous-time system model to discrete-time and knows the effect of aliasing.

The student can analyze (periodic and non-periodic continuous-time and discrete-time) signals in the frequency domain, knows how signals are sampled, can choose an appropriate sampling frequency, knows the concept of leakage and knows how this can be avoided.

syllabus_topics: M1: Modeling of systems with and without feedback
M2: System analysis (continuous- & discrete-time, focus on single-input single-output systems)
Physical models of systems, linearization and block diagrams
M3: Analysis and design of controllers based on feedback and feedforward
Stability analysis based on Bode & Nyquist plot
Design of classical controllers (P, PID, lead/lag) using the frequency characteristic of the system
Design of controllers based on state feedback, including state estimator
Design of feedforward for different types of reference signals
Analysis of the properties and stability of feedback systems
Design of classical feedback controllers (proportional, proportional-derivative, lead and lag compensators) and design of feedforward
Design of feedback controllers based on state feedback including state estimator
Analysis of signals, sampling and discretization

assessment_methods.method: Written examination during the examination period

assessment_rules: The exam consists of three questions, each potentially with multiple sub-questions. The weighting for the three questions is equal. Any rounding is done according to the usual rule, but in case of deficiencies in at least two of the three questions, rounding is always downwards. Only the officially agreed calculator may be used. The two formularies provided on TOLEDO may be used, printed out by the student and brought to the exam without any notes.
institution: KU Leuven - Faculty of Engineering Science
degree: Bachelor in de ingenieurswetenschappen (Bachelor of Engineering Science, Leuven)
